review_candidates.title: Vice President of Finance and Operations
review_candidates.description: About The Myelodysplastic Syndromes Foundation The Myelodysplastic Syndromes (MDS) Foundation is the global nonprofit leader dedicated to improving the lives of patients and families affected by MDS through patient support, education, research, advocacy, and strategic collaboration. We serve as a trusted resource for patients, caregivers, healthcare professionals, researchers, and industry partners worldwide while working to accelerate better outcomes and, ultimately, cures. Position Overview The Vice President of Finance and Operations leads the MDS Foundation's financial strategy and core operational functions, ensuring sound financial stewardship, operational excellence, regulatory compliance, and the infrastructure needed to support informed decision-making, organizational transparency, and long-term sustainability. As a key member of the senior leadership team, the Vice President serves as a strategic partner to the CEO and Board of Directors during an important phase of organizational growth. The role provides executive oversight of financial planning and analysis, budgeting, reporting, audit, compliance, and operational systems, while developing the scalable processes, controls, and infrastructure necessary to support the Foundation's mission and long-term strategic priorities. The Vice President will ensure the Foundation's financial and operational data are translated into meaningful insights that support strategic planning, organizational performance, and decision-making. The ideal candidate is an entrepreneurial, strategic builder who thrives in a dynamic, mission-driven environment, combining big-picture vision with a hands-on approach to execution. They will strengthen the Foundation's financial and operational capabilities by driving continuous improvement, enhancing organizational effectiveness, and building the systems, processes, and insights that enable sustainable growth and greater mission impact. Key Responsibilities Financial Strategy Lead the Foundation's financial strategy by developing long-term financial plans, projections, scenario analyses, and cash-flow models that support organizational sustainability, liquidity, and growth. Serve as a strategic advisor to the CEO and Board of Directors, providing financial analysis, modeling, and insights to inform organizational decisions. Develop meaningful financial and operational performance metrics that support organizational accountability and continuous improvement. Budgeting, Forecasting, and Financial Planning Lead development and oversight of the annual budget and multi-year financial plans. Design and implement best-in-class budgeting and forecasting processes, transitioning from legacy or ad hoc approaches to more rigorous, forward-looking planning. Monitor financial performance through forecasting, variance analysis, and scenario planning, proactively identifying risks and opportunities. Financial Reporting, Transparency, and Controls Build financial reporting frameworks and dashboards to improve visibility, decision-making, and organizational accountability. Prepare and present financial materials for Board and Finance/Audit Committee meetings; serve as financial expert at those meetings. Strengthen financial controls by assessing existing accounting practices and implementing robust internal controls, policies, and documentation to safeguard organizational assets. Accounting, Audit, and Compliance Provide executive oversight of all accounting functions, including general ledger, accounts payable and receivable, payroll accounting, and month-end and year-end close. Ensure compliance with GAAP, IRS regulations, nonprofit accounting standards, and all applicable federal and state requirements. Serve as primary liaison to external auditors and oversee the annual audit, Form 990 preparation, and other tax filings. Operational Excellence Assess and strengthen accounting infrastructure and close processes to improve efficiency, accuracy, and scalability. Lead the Foundation's payroll and benefits administration through effective management of the PEO relationship, ensuring compliance, accuracy, and an exceptional employee experience. Provide financial and operational oversight of employee benefits, including health, retirement, and related programs, in partnership with external vendors. The project responds to the prioritisation of women’s economic empowerment by expanding market access for Women-owned Businesses (WOBs) and Gender Responsive Enterprises (GREs) through procurement opportunities. WRT tackles the structural gender inequities that exist within the global procurement market in which WOBs secure only one per cent of spending worldwide. By introducing and advancing increased market access through gender-responsive procurement (GRP), WRT operates with the overall objective to empower more women to equally access, lead, and benefit from expanded market opportunities in the Mekong subregion. In its second phase , WE RISE Together Phase 2 (WRT 2.0) - (1 March 2025 to 28 February 2029) is funded and supported by the Australian Government through the Mekong–Australia Partnership (MAP) and implemented by UN Women to advance Gender-Responsive Procurement (GRP) in the Mekong Subregion across Cambodia, the Lao People’s Democratic Republic (Lao PDR), Thailand, and Viet Nam . We are a market-leading independent power producer and service provider, serving utilities, corporations, industries, communities, institutions, and investors with reliable, low-carbon energy solutions that help meet growing demand. From developing and building scalable wind (onshore and offshore), solar, storage (battery and pumped storage hydro), smart EV charging, microgrids, green hydrogen, and transmission projects, to maximizing performance and profitability through skilled operations and maintenance and innovative asset optimization, our teams deliver expert solutions along the entire value chain—from origination to commercial operation. Be a part of an innovative and collaborative team environment that fosters our goal of delivering renewable solutions to lead the transition to a sustainable energy future. Benefits & Perks EDF power solutions offers best-in-class employee benefits, including the following: Competitive bonus incentives. This position is eligible for our annual bonus program. Comprehensive health coverage. We provide low-cost health & wellness coverage for employees and their eligible dependents. Rewarding 401k. We provide a generous matching contribution. We Are Also Proud To Offer Favorable paid time off programs, including paid parental leave after one year of service. Rewarding learning & career development and advancement opportunities. Supportive mentorship & buddy programs. Salary Range : The full pay range for this role is $120,800 to $201,300 annually, and the good faith estimated starting pay for this position upon hire is $145,000 to $170,000 annually. We generally base our salary decisions on factors including but not limited to, relevant work and leadership experience, education, demonstrated performance, internal equity, and in some cases, geographic location. Scope of Job : The Senior EPC Project Manager (Sr. EPC PM) is responsible for leading EPC execution activities in accordance with EDFR’s safety, quality, and management standards, for Utility-Scale Solar, On-Shore Wind, and Energy Storage Projects within EDFR’s portfolio. They will work with cross-functional teams and subject-matter-experts to manage EPC contractors from contractor selection, through execution, completion and project handover, and support advanced stage project development activities such as EPC services procurement and contracting. Responsibilities EPC Project Execution Manage the implementation of the EPC contract and the project execution plan. Manage and work closely with the EDF site team, internal and external subject matter experts. Accountable for project safety, quality, budget, and schedule control. Lead or participate in day-to-day coordination activities (Plan-of-day meetings, monthly meetings, engineering meetings). Accountable for implementation of transport and logistics plan with respect to Owner Provided Equipment. Accountable for Testing and Commissioning plan preparation and implementation. Perform project close-out activities, such as claims settlement, lessons learned, cost and schedule analysis. EPC Contracting Accountable for negotiation of technical and commercial contract exhibits. Coordinate internal exhibits review with subject matter experts. Contribute to negotiation of the EPC contract. EPC Services Procurement Support RFP Bid evaluation and contractors’ selection. Continuous Improvement Initiatives: Contribute to or lead initiatives such as improving processes and developing tools. Evaluate feasibility and impact of LCOE reduction initiatives. Evaluate and incorporate lessons learned. Other duties as assigned. Supervision of Others : 1-2 direct, 5-7 indirect. Working Conditions : Approximately 80% of the time is spent in the office environment, using computers (frequent use of MS Office Suite), phones, and general office equipment. Approximately 20% of the time is spent in the field nationally and internationally, visiting projects, evaluating sites, and meeting project team members and various stakeholders. Fiscal Responsibilities : EPC Budget Qualifications Qualifications & Experience : Minimum of 6 years of relevant experience including comprehensive and diversified knowledge of the construction industry, renewables EPC market, including knowledge of renewables industry best management practices, codes, standards, and engineering principles. Extensive experience working and negotiating with EPC Contractors on contracts exceeding $100M. Experience executing projects in accordance with project management principles. Experience working in cross-functional organization structure. Experience leading a project execution team. Education Bachelor’s degree in engineering, construction management, or equivalent. Skills/Knowledge/Abilities Strong negotiation and communication skills with counterparties of varied interests and levels of technical and business expertise. Strong organizational, leadership, and management skills with the ability to effectively collaborate with geographically disperse, cross functional team members (i.e., engineering, construction, program management, developers, etc.) Adaptability to changing market conditions and shifting business priorities. Knowledge of renewable power plant design (electrical, civil, etc.) Knowledge of renewable energy project offtake and financing structures. Knowledge of national and regional regulatory environment. Highly motivated, self-starter, ability to work well with others and be a good team player. Proficiency in English (spoken and written), and with MS Office Suite (Excel, Project, Power Point). Physical Requirements Ability to sit, stand, walk on uneven surfaces, visit job sites.

review_candidates.title: Senior Associate, Construction & Infrastructure Disputes Lawyer
review_candidates.description: 5+ years' PAE Genuine and approachable partners Major projects focused disputes We represent a major Australian law firm comprising lawyers across a number of Australian offices, and including a significant global network. As an upshot of growth, the Sydney office are now looking to hire a Senior Associate level construction disputes lawyer. Construction, Projects and Infrastructure The Sydney Construction, Projects and Infrastructure group work on some of the most significant infrastructure, construction, engineering, mining and renewable energy projects in the Asia-Pacific region for a range of public and private participants. As a market leading practice, you can expect to work with individuals at the top of their game. Position Description This is a position which will provide unparalleled opportunities for progression, mentorship and skill development in this area of law. You will act for principally major contractors on a mix of dispute resolution including litigation, arbitration, mediation and expert determination across infrastructure (transport and social), utilities (water, power, gas and telecommunications), government (defence, rail) and renewable energy. This is a great opportunity for a driven and talented senior-level lawyer who wants to be part of a growing and busy team with genuine progression opportunities in a market-leading practice. Requirements You will be a lawyer with most likely 5+ years' experience, in back-end construction law or a disputes lawyer looking to specialise in construction. In addition, you will: have excellent communication skills, both written and verbal as well as people skills have strong attention to detail with well-developed analytical skills be wanting to be part of a highly energetic and driven team. In return, you will be rewarded with an impressive remuneration package, excellent career development opportunities and a great team environment. Contact For further information, please contact Andrew Rees on +61 (0) 404 835 853 or arees@montgomeryadvisory.com.au To take your application one step further, register your details via the ‘Register Now’ button on our website to be added directly onto our database. Visit www.montgomeryadvisory.com.au. We are committed to fostering a truly inclusive process for all candidates who wish to apply. If you need assistance or adjustments to fully participate in the application process, please contact admin@montgomeryadvisory.com.au.

review_candidates.title: Sales AGENTS
review_candidates.description: Company Description Ngao Credit Limited is a non-deposit taking microfinance institution focused on providing accessible financial services to a diverse range of clients. The organization is dedicated to offering unique, tailor-made financial solutions that address individual client needs. Ngao Credit emphasizes speed and efficiency, working to deliver services in the shortest time possible. The company values client satisfaction and strives to build long-term relationships based on trust and reliability. Role Description This full-time on-site role as a Sales Agent is based in Mombasa. The Sales Agent will identify and approach potential clients, explain Ngao Credit’s financial products, and guide clients through the application and approval processes. Daily tasks include following up on leads, maintaining accurate records of client interactions, and meeting set sales targets. The role also involves providing after-sales support, collaborating with team members, and participating in training sessions to stay informed about new products and compliance requirements. Qualifications Strong Communication and Customer Service skills to engage clients effectively and build lasting relationships. Proven Sales skills, including lead generation, negotiation, and closing deals. Basic understanding of Insurance products and the ability to explain them clearly to clients. Ability to participate in and apply Training to improve product knowledge and sales techniques. Goal-oriented mindset with the ability to meet and exceed sales targets. Good organizational and record-keeping skills for managing client information. Proficiency in basic computer applications and use of mobile technology. Previous experience in microfinance, banking, or related financial services is an added advantage.
